issues.decision: Replace the combined stall/head-gasket card with recall 18V-049's exact gasoline-engine software condition and exclusions.

evidence.label: FCA Recall U01 / NHTSA 18V-049 - Engine Stall Due to Software Issue

trims: Certain gasoline Pacifica vehicles in recall U01 / 18V-049; PHEV vehicles are excluded and applicability must be confirmed by VIN
after.title: Engine Can Stall After Crankshaft-Signal Synchronization Loss (Recall 18V-049)
after.description: FCA recall U01 / NHTSA 18V-049 covers certain 2017 Chrysler Pacifica gasoline vehicles built with engine-control software vulnerable to losing synchronization with the crankshaft-position signal. The engine can stall without prior warning. The official population excludes 2017 Pacifica PHEVs and later vehicles built with the updated software; this recall does not establish the former card's head-gasket claim.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall U01. An authorized Chrysler dealer updates the engine-control software at no charge. A current stall still requires diagnosis because an open recall does not prove every stall has this cause; move out of traffic if possible and arrange professional service after a loss of motive power.
symptoms: VIN is included in recall U01

citations.title: FCA Recall U01 / NHTSA 18V-049 - Engine Stall Due to Software Issue

after.contentUpdateSummary: Removed the unsupported head-gasket aggregation and narrowed the card to recall 18V-049's exact 2017 gasoline population, software mechanism, exclusions, and no-charge remedy.

issues.decision: Replace the stale 2017-2021 battery-fire aggregation with the current FCA/NHTSA recall populations and safety instructions through model year 2022.

evidence.label: FCA Recall 73B / NHTSA 24V-536 - 2017-2018 Pacifica PHEV High-Voltage Battery
FCA Recall 72B / NHTSA 24V-538 - 2019-2021 Pacifica PHEV High-Voltage Battery
FCA Recall 52D / NHTSA 26V-362 - 2020-2022 Pacifica PHEV Battery Fire Risk

trims: Pacifica Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicles included in recall 73B / 24V-536, 72B / 24V-538, or 52D / 26V-362; verify each VIN
after.title: PHEV High-Voltage Battery Can Cause a Fire While Parked (Recalls 24V-536, 24V-538, and 26V-362)
after.description: Current FCA campaigns cover separate VIN-specific Pacifica PHEV battery populations with a fire risk even while parked and switched off: recall 73B / 24V-536 covers certain 2017-2018 vehicles previously remedied under 22V-077; recall 72B / 24V-538 covers certain 2019-2021 vehicles; and recall 52D / 26V-362 covers certain 2020-2022 vehicles. The campaigns do not mean every Pacifica in these model years is affected.
after.solution: Until every applicable recall is completed, follow FCA's safety direction: do not charge the vehicle and park it outdoors away from structures and other vehicles. Check the VIN for all current campaigns. Authorized dealers update battery-control software and inspect the high-voltage battery pack, replacing the pack when required, at no charge. If smoke, heat, odor, or fire is suspected, keep away and contact emergency services.
symptoms: VIN included in a current PHEV battery-fire recall
Possible battery thermal event while parked or switched off
Battery warning or condition identified by the recall diagnostic procedure

issues.decision: Anchor the PHEV transmission-wiring card to recall 23V-010's exact model-year scope, failure mechanisms, and remedy.

evidence.label: FCA Recall 03A / NHTSA 23V-010 - Loss of Motive Power

trims: Pacifica Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicles included in recall 03A / 23V-010; verify by VIN
after.title: PHEV Transmission Connector or Rotor-Bearing Defect Can Cause Shutdown (Recall 23V-010)
after.description: FCA recall 03A / NHTSA 23V-010 covers certain 2017-2023 Chrysler Pacifica PHEVs. FCA states that an internal transmission wiring-connector short or a rotor-bearing installation defect can cause an unexpected engine shutdown and loss of motive power without prior warning.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall 03A and have an authorized Chrysler dealer complete the current remedy. FCA's instructions call for Power Inverter Module software and, when applicable, instrument-cluster and engine-control software updates; FCA also provides an unlimited-time, unlimited-mile warranty extension for affected customers who receive defect-related messaging and require transmission replacement. Recall and warranty applicability are VIN-specific.
symptoms: Defect-related warning message identified by FCA service procedures

citations.title: FCA Recall 03A / NHTSA 23V-010 - Loss of Motive Power

after.contentUpdateSummary: Anchored the PHEV wiring card to recall 23V-010's exact model years, two documented transmission mechanisms, software remedy, and related warranty extension.
